title: Attorney General of North Dakota

context.text: This is a rematch of 2022, when Wrigley defeated Lamb; the North Dakota Monitor reports Lamb received about 31% of the vote. Lamb later lost the 2024 state auditor race.
Wrigley was unopposed in the June 9, 2026 Republican primary (99.2%, write-ins excepted) and Lamb in the Democratic-NPL primary (99.7%).
The North Dakota Secretary of State's certified 2026 General Election candidate list shows two candidates for Attorney General: Drew Wrigley and Tim Lamb (listed on the ballot as Tim Lamb).

candidates.name: Drew Wrigley
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 9, 2026 Republican primary with no declared opponent.

record.text: On September 25, 2026 his office issued several summary legal opinions to public bodies, including one concluding that the White Shield Public School District violated open records law.
Urged consumers to claim compensation for inflated generic drug prices.

candidates.name: Timothy Lamb
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 9, 2026 Democratic-NPL nomination; endorsed at the March 7 state convention.

priorities.text: Create a criminal justice review panel, a citizen review board for fraud, and a round table for attorneys and judges to suggest improvements to the legal system.

sources.title: North Dakota Democrats endorse several statewide candidates

researchNotes: Slate: confirmed against the North Dakota Secretary of State's certified 2026 General Election candidate list. Neither candidate has a campaign website or questionnaire that could be fetched, so no issue stances are recorded. Lamb's background draws on a 2022 University of North Dakota Law blog post and the North Dakota Monitor. Wrigley's record items come from the Attorney General's news page.
